result.title: Gradient-Free Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision Models via Agentic Coding
result.summary: Adapting a vision model to new classes from a few labeled images usually relies on gradient fine-tuning, which is unstable with so few images. We ask whether a coding agent can replace gradient descent for this task. We propose the Agent edit, a method in which a coding agent writes a program that sets the new class weights in the class head of a frozen COCO-trained detector, with no gradient step. The agent runs the detector on the labeled images a limited number of times and sees how much its edit lowers COCO mAP; the program rebuilds the weights without the agent. In the same head and with the same labels, the Agent edit outperforms full-decoder fine-tuning at five shots on 2 of four fine-grained sets, by 11.2 and 12.3 F1 points, and ties on the rest. At ten shots, fine-tuning ties with or outperforms it. Moreover, when the new classes are scored jointly with the COCO classes, the AP of the COCO class to which they belong falls by up to 33.3 points, and limiting that loss lowers F1 on the new classes. Most of the agent's programs share three parts, which we write as a formula that needs no agent. A classifier on frozen backbone features reaches a higher F1 than every method inside the head on every set. Hence a coding agent can replace gradient descent only in part: inside the head and at five shots.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「Agent edit」：让编码 agent 在无梯度更新的情况下编写程序，直接设定冻结的 COCO 检测器类头中新类别的权重，仅用少量标注图与有限次 mAP 反馈迭代，并发现多数 agent 程序可归约为三个部分构成的、无需 agent 的公式。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以有限反馈的代码编辑替代梯度优化、再把 agent 程序提炼为固定公式」的模式，可能为 LVR 中的搜索与验证、贡献分配以及把搜索摊销进固定计算提供线索；但任务本身不涉及多模态推理状态，需人工核查可迁移性。
